When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the find compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` against a falsy value, so it can never match and the fallback yields undefined — whereas the pre-diff code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Same dead-fallback pattern appears in deleteEvent. This is a verifiable regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), the fallback `find` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match any normal `externalId`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. This is a dead/incorrect fallback introduced by the diff (previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when it was a single object). The same pattern appears in `deleteEvent` too, and can lead to an undefined calendarId unless separately defaulted elsewhere.
